detail.title: Operational Foundations of Causal Memory (Revised)
detail.summary: Persistent physical states function as operational memory only when they provide predictive sufficiency relative to a specified coarse-graining scale. The thermodynamic maintenance of these states—specifically erasure and retention—is modulated by nonequilibrium conditions, including nonreciprocal couplings and potential energy differences between reservoirs.
detail.reason: Revision necessary to synthesize new thermodynamic evidence regarding information engines and renormalization group approaches to coarse-graining.
